title: A ring of zeros
starter:
%x  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=0
%y  = buffer 16 dtype=f32 slot=1
# x is 2x2. Store the 4x4 grid with x in the middle and zeros all around.
%v  = load %x
%m  = reshape %v shape=[2 2]
%p  = pad %m pads=[2 0 2 0]
%f  = reshape %p shape=[16]
%s  = store %y %f
%y1 = after %y %s
hints: The starter's grid is 4x4, but x sits in the bottom-right corner. Where do the zeros go?
`pads` lists a left and a right amount per axis: `[top bottom left right]` for a 2D value.
explain: `pad` takes `(left, right)` per axis, so `[1 1 1 1]` adds one row above and below and one column on each side: 2x2 becomes 4x4 with x at rows and columns 1 and 2. The fill is `0.0`, the f32 zero. A `-0.0` or `nan` inside x is copied as is. Only the new cells are zero.
